thread:
Incident Bot: ✨ INCIDENT OPENED: prefix-eviction spike -> KV cache misses. Paging SRE Oncall. Priority: P1.
SRE Oncall: I’m on it — switching to incident channel. brief?
Alice M: tl;dr: sudden jump in kv_miss rate starting ~10:00 UTC. 95p latency for /v1/generate up 3x. Correlates with prefix-eviction job that ran at 09:58.
Bob K: seeing increased fallback to disk for a subset of tenants, error 503s for streaming connections. heavy-tenant-42 most impacted.
EngRuntime: graph queries: ```sum(rate(kv_prefix_evictions_total[5m])) by (shard)
sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le)
``` looks like eviction churn + rewarm thrash.
SRE Oncall: immediate mitigations?
Alice M: propose: 1) disable prefix-eviction job for now 2) enable KV-prefetch bypass (serve directly from origin for correctness) 3) apply tenant-level rate-sculpt for heavy-tenant-42 so others unaffected.
EngRuntime: I can flip the eviction job via kconfig. command: ```POST https://deploy.internal/ops/feature-toggle
Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN
{"name":"prefix_eviction","state":"off","reason":"emergency-mitigation"}```
EngRuntime: for the KV-prefetch bypass we have runtime flag `prefix_kv_bypass=true` per pool. Hotpatch command: ```ssh relay-ctrl-01
sudo /opt/runtime/bin/rollout --pool=shared-models --set prefix_kv_bypass=true --reason "eviction-mitigation"```
Bob K: I’ll start traffic-sculpt on edge for heavy-tenant-42: `edgectl rate-limit set tenant:heavy-tenant-42 100rps` then reduce to 50rps if needed.
SRE Oncall: CS Lead — which customers are impacted? any enterprise SLAs at risk?
CS Lead: Notified: acme-corp, finserve-pro, and edu-labs. acme-corp reported degraded interactive latency, CS ticket 78910 opened. Enterprise SLA threshold approaching for finserve-pro — they’re on a latency SLA.
SRE Oncall: OK prioritize finserve-pro guardrail. Bob, please set a hard quota for finserve-pro at safe baseline.
Bob K: setting quota: `rctl tenant set finserve-pro --qps 20 --burst 40` — applying now.
Infra Bot: rollout plan created: rollout/1959876543/prefix-bypass v1 -> canary 2 hosts -> full. ETA canary finish 60s.
EngRuntime: canary applied to pool `canary-shard-3`. Observing metrics… kv_miss rate on canary down ~70%.
Alice M: logs from model-server: ```[10:12:34] WARN prefix_evict: eviction_count=1200 rewarm_attempts=340
[10:12:35] INFO prefix_bypass: active=true pool=canary-shard-3
``` looks promising.
SRE Oncall: start progressive rollback of eviction job across control plane — if bypass holds, we keep eviction off and schedule safe rewarm.
Bob K: traffic-sculpt update: heavy-tenant-42 reduced to 30rps; overall error rate for /v1/generate dropping.
CS Lead: acme-corp reports partial recovery via websocket; still seeing some timeouts but improved. sent interim status email.
SRE Oncall: monitor for 15m. If stable, we’ll convert bypass to 30m hotfix and plan postmortem. Assigning follow-up to EngRuntime + Alice.
EngRuntime: will add shielding: tenant-level prefix cache caps to prevent single-tenant thrash. prototype patch: `prefix_shield_cap=5000` per tenant.
Alice M: also adding metric alert: `kv_miss_rate > 50/s for 5m` -> page SRE again.
Infra Bot: canary finished green. full rollout started (10 hosts).
SRE Oncall: metrics look stable at 10:25 UTC; 95p latency back to baseline for most tenants. closing active paging window but keeping incident channel open for 1h.
Bob K: leaving notes in ops-runbook and added temporary rate limits for 3 tenants.
CS Lead: updated customer list and close-looped on support tickets.
SRE Oncall: next steps: 1) postmortem 72h 2) implement tenant shielding + backpressure 3) safe rewarm strategy for prefixes 4) run Chaos test for eviction job at low traffic.
Alice M: saved CLI snippets to /ops/incidents/1959876543/playbook.md and marked as hotpatch history.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status -> monitoring. tags: prefix, kv, mitigation, hotpatch.
SRE Oncall: handing off to Bob for monitoring window. I’m off pager in 20m. If anything flares, ping oncall.
Bob K: acknowledged — I have the pager. Thanks team :thumbsup:
